game.summary: Wired the pure ruins into MatchRoom (protocol v8). Every source now starts locked (the rubbings-theft unlock-all is removed). The ruins are dealt from their own master-secret seed (deriveSeed 'ruins'). The first solve's sources-unlocked calls unlockSource, and each solver's gold-awarded calls grantGold (reason ruin, key String(island)). The room reports presence every tick in play, so casting off, a duel or a disconnect closes the session, and a leave closes it at once. New zod-validated messages: open-ruin/ruin-clue (the clue goes to the opener only, strictly parsed) and answer-ruin/ruin-result (idempotent by request id, the last 16 remembered; opens and answers share a cap of 8/s; read only in play). Private status carries the ruin state, session and lockout. Per-island ruin markers are view-filtered by sight. Test-only ruins (env PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_RUINS, the next-match route, MatchTuning.testRuins) open islands or pin a kind through derived ruins:<n> seeds. Integration quickStart and the browser server open every island, so theft-loop and full-match use the test-only unlock. Web: ruinPanel.ts (tablets with inscriptions, 4x4 grid, keys 1-6 / arrows / WASD / Backspace / Enter / Escape, clicks, lockout countdown, '+40 gold' and unlock lines), R in the HUD, neutral helm while the panel is open. Carried P2s: recordedOutcomes is bounded to 64 (outcomes.ts, with a unit test), and the banner re-arm and auto-hide have fake-timer tests plus rows 286-288 in match-online-coverage.md. docs/ruins-online-coverage.md has 188 rows (159 tested, 15 equivalent, 14 removed), each built by deleting the branch on scratch copies in parallel lanes. Checks executed here: npm run typecheck (pass), npm run test:unit (1311 pass), npm run test:integration (115 pass, 175 s), npm run build (pass, including the smoke), the full playwright suite with the JSON reporter (13 pass), and check-report (all 11 scenarios ok).
open_assumptions: An island is 'in sight' when the nearest point of its rectangle is within the sight radius. The marker is placed at the island's centre.
Opening a ruin that someone else already unlocked is still offered (R), because solving it pays that player's own 40 gold.
docs/ruins.md (not an owned path) still says the ruins aren't wired into MatchRoom. It needs a one-line update by its owner.

The e2e scenarios other than ruin-solve run with every island open (PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_RUINS=*=open in the Playwright config). ruin-solve and the navigation test ask for locked ruins through the next-match route.

# Decisions: ruins-online

From the operator session of 2026-09-25. The operator asked for the launch. The assistant settled the choices below, and they're recorded in `operator-logs/decisions-overnight.md`.

## Decisions

- The pure ruins rules on `main` (`packages/simulation/src/ruins`, `packages/content/src/ruins`) are used through their exports and aren't owned. The room passes `createRuins` a ruins seed derived from the match's master secret (the per-system HMAC seeds from `match-online`). That seed is independent of the ledger seed, so clues can't reveal the ledger's layout, and the pure module doesn't need to change.
- Every island's sources lock at match start. The first solve unlocks them for everyone (decision #23), and `rubbings-theft`'s stopgap of unlocking every source goes away.
- R opens the ruin while moored. It's a new key, shown in the HUD. E stays "hold to collect" and J stays "grapple".
- Every solver earns 40 gold once per ruin, through `grantGold` (reason `ruin`, key `String(island)`).
- The existing browser scenarios (`theft-loop`, `full-match`) unlock their islands with a test-only setting, so they stay about the loop they test. `ruin-solve` proves the real UI.
- The committed branch → test table (`docs/ruins-online-coverage.md`) is required from the start (decision #49).
- The two P2s from `match-online`'s approving reviews are folded in: the bounded `outcomes` array, and the banner re-arm and auto-hide tests.

## Assumptions

- Everything in `features/match-online/` and its fixes stands.
- The ruin kind per island is dealt by the pure module. Tests pin it with a test-only setting.

## Deferred

- Fruit pedestals and kits online (`fruit-kits-online`), rumors and the journal (`intel-online`), and shops (`economy-online`) come next, in that order.

concerns.message: The plan says the browser tests 'pin the ruin kind for the island through a test-only setting', but `createRuins` takes no kind option. It picks the kind by drawing from the seed (`drawInt(source, 2)` in ruins/state.ts:111), and `generateSequence`/`generateNavigation` are not exported from `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/ruins`. The only way to pin a kind through the exports is to choose the ruins seed: search derived seeds until `createRuins(...).ruins[i].puzzle.kind` matches, or pin a test ruins seed the way `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_FINAL_SECRET` pins the final island.
concerns.consequence: A worker who reads 'pin the kind' as needing a new `kind` option in the pure module stops with `blocked` under the Stop rule ('a pure module change is truly required'). A worker who instead hand-builds a `SequencePuzzle` without the module's uniqueness check can end up with a clue that has several answers, so the browser test's solver fails.

concerns.message: Arrows/WASD are also the sailing keys. In step.ts:54-59, any throttle input whose direction differs from `mooredThrottle` casts a moored ship off, so W/S/Up/Down do it. If the client keeps sending helm input while the navigation panel is open, the ship leaves the dock. `reportPresence` then closes the session, and every answer is refused (`not-at-ruin`/`no-session`). The plan never says the panel takes the keyboard and the helm goes neutral while it's open.
concerns.consequence: Navigation ruins can't be solved in the real client. If Playwright's `keyboard.press` is too short for the server to sample, the navigation browser test may pass anyway while real players get cast off every time.

concerns.message: The ruins module has no disconnect or reconnect operation. docs/ruins.md:47 says the room reports presence 'when a ship moors or casts off' and when `reserveDuel` puts a player in a duel. A disconnect has to be reported as `island: null` while the ship stays moored. A reconnect, the loser's respawn moored at a dock (`returnShip` with a dock) and a settled duel (back to `inDuel: false`) are not moor events at all.
concerns.consequence: If presence is only reported on those events, a reconnected, respawned or post-duel player at a dock gets 'not-at-ruin' or 'in-duel' on R until they cast off and moor again. It would also pass the planned integration tests unless one of them reopens after a reconnect or respawn. Fix: every world tick, derive presence as (connected && docked island ≥ 0 ? island : null, held in a duel), and let the module drop unchanged reports as duplicates. Map dock island -1 to null, since `reportPresence` rejects negative islands as invalid and would leave the old session open.

concerns.message: `open-ruin`/`answer-ruin` arrive through `onMessage`, outside `worldTick`. `worldTick` stops everything once `flow.end !== null`, and ship control is gated on `inPlay()`. The ruins module knows nothing about match phases. `receiveTheftChoice` shows that message handlers rely on the pure module for gating.
concerns.consequence: A player moored at a dock in the lobby or ready countdown could solve before control starts. A player with a session open at the end could solve after the match ends and mint 40 gold into the ledger after the results are frozen, and the HUD gold would disagree with the results table. Gate open and answer on `inPlay()`, and add a row for that branch to the table.

concerns.message: All browser scenarios share one `webServer`, whose test settings are server-wide environment variables (`playwright.config.ts`). `theft-loop` and `full-match` need their islands unlocked (both use Palm Key and Ember Rock, islands 0 and 1). `ruin-solve` and the navigation test need locked islands with pinned kinds. A global 'unlock all ruins' env makes `ruin-solve` impossible on the same server. Every existing integration setup that collects (rubbings, claim, endings, reveals, flowReports, seaDuelSetup, matchFlowSetup) also breaks once sources start locked.
concerns.consequence: Rework and flaky ordering if this is found late, or a 'next match' endpoint whose pending state leaks between specs. Use one island-scoped setting instead, e.g. `unlock=0,1;sequence=2;navigation=3`, parsed in protocol, applied in `createMatchLedger`/`createRuins`, and passed through `matchTuning` in the integration setups.

concerns.message: The branch table requires deleting every branch on a scratch copy and running tests in parallel batches. The Playwright config uses fixed ports (2593/5393, `reuseExistingServer: false`), and several runs share this machine. UI branches whose only failing test is a browser test can't be batched in parallel. Taken together with the server wiring, protocol, DOM panel, two new browser tests, the integration churn and the two carried P2s, this doesn't fit easily in a three-hour worker. `match-online` needed two fix rounds.
concerns.consequence: The worker runs out of time on the table, or marks UI branches as covered only by slow sequential e2e runs. Put the panel's logic in pure web models (clue rendering, answer entry, lockout countdown, HUD ruin state) so that nearly every UI branch fails a vitest unit test, and deletions stay cheap and parallel.

concerns.message: The browser test must 'derive the answer from the displayed clue only'. The sequence clue is English from `tabletText` with 8 relation phrasings ('comes somewhere after', 'does not come last', 'in the middle'…). A solver that parses sentences is brittle, and one that reads a pinned seed's answer defeats the requirement.
concerns.consequence: Either a flaky browser solver, or a reviewer rejecting a test that doesn't read the page. Render each tablet as DOM text plus structured attributes (`data-symbol`, `data-relation`, `data-other`, `data-position`), and each grid cell with its role. The test can then brute-force the 120 permutations or run a BFS from what the page shows.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Keep the design, but make three things mechanical instead of event-driven. (1) Derive ruin presence every world tick from the ship's dock, connection and duel hold, and gate the handlers on `inPlay()`. This removes separate hooks for moor, cast-off, disconnect, reconnect, respawn and duel end. (2) Use one island-scoped test setting on the shared server, e.g. `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_RUINS=unlock=0,1;sequence=2;navigation=3`. It covers theft-loop, full-match and both ruin tests on one server without endpoints between tests. Pin the kinds with a seed search over the exported `createRuins`, so no pure module changes. (3) Build the ruin panel as a DOM overlay driven by pure web models. While it's open it takes the keyboard and the helm sends neutral, and the models' unit tests cover the UI branches in the table.
challenge.cheap_experiment: A 15-minute script against the current exports, before any worker starts. Call `createRuins({ seed, islands: [0..3].map(i => ({ island: i, sourceIds: [`source-${i}-0`, `source-${i}-1`] })) })` for seeds 0..200. Record each island's kind, the time per call, and the first seed with island 2 = sequence and island 3 = navigation. For every sequence ruin, run the planned test-side solver on `tabletText` output, or on structured hint fields, and confirm it finds exactly the answer. Separately, place a ship at a dock in a dev room, moor it with E, send one frame of W, and confirm it casts off (`dock` becomes `NOT_DOCKED`). The results show whether pinning the kind through the exports is cheap, whether the solver approach is reliable, and whether the panel must neutralize the helm.

game.task:
# Task: game

## Goal

Make the islands' rubbings something you earn with your head, not just your hands. Each regular island's sources start **locked** behind its ruin (§3). A captain moored at the island opens the ruin and reads the clue at the site:
- **a three-symbol sequence:** six carved tablets with relational hints;
- **a small navigation puzzle:** a 4 × 4 grid.

They enter the answer. The first player to solve it unlocks the island's rubbings for everyone, and every solver earns 40 gold once. A wrong answer locks that player out for 3 s. A fresh ruin should take about 20–40 s including the 6 s rubbing, so the UI must make the clue easy to read and the answer quick to enter, and guessing must be worse than reading. The pure rules are on `main` (`packages/simulation/src/ruins`, `docs/ruins.md`); this feature wires them in.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §3 ("Exploration activities"), §11 (fresh ruin completion: 40 gold once per player per ruin) and §16 (hidden information).
- Read `docs/ruins.md` (`createRuins`, `openRuin`, `answerRuin`, leaving and duel handling, `clueFor`, the `sources-unlocked` and `gold-awarded` events, lockouts per player and ruin), `docs/objectives.md` (`unlockSource`, `grantGold` with reason `ruin` and key `String(island)`), `docs/architecture.md`, and the room and client as `match-online` left them: the master secret and per-system seeds, the lobby and phases, and how collection works at docks.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. The pure modules and their content aren't owned: use them through their exports, and report `blocked` naming the gap if a change is truly needed. Server authoritative, zod-validated messages, protocol version bump. One Phaser game per page. Tests drive input like players do, and the browser test reads the clue from the page and solves it the way a player would.
- Hidden information: a ruin's clue goes only to players moored at that island with an open session. The answer never leaves the server in any form. Other players see only whether the island is unlocked, when they're in sight of it or moored there.

## Design (settled)

- **Seeds:** the ruins get their own seed derived from the match's master secret, the `match-online` mechanism. This fixes the ruins reviewer's finding that `seed ^ const` let clues leak the ledger seed.
- **Locking:** at match start every ledger source is locked (`rubbings-theft` unlocked them all as a stopgap; remove that). Collection at an island needs its ruin solved by anyone: the first solve's `sources-unlocked` calls `unlockSource` for each.
- **Interaction:** moored at an island whose ruin this player hasn't solved, pressing **R** (a new key, shown in the HUD) opens the ruin panel. `openRuin` returns only the clue. Casting off, entering a duel or disconnecting closes the session, as the rules define. The panel shows the clue clearly:
  - **sequence:** six tablets with their symbols and hint sentences, and the answer entered by clicking three symbols in order, or keys 1–6, with an undo;
  - **navigation:** the grid drawn with start, goal and blocked cells, and the answer entered with the arrow keys or WASD, shown as a path, with an undo.
  - Submit sends `answer-ruin`: zod-validated, rate-limited, idempotent by request id.
  - A wrong answer shows the 3 s lockout counting down.
  - Solving shows "Ruin solved: +40 gold", and, if first, "The island's rubbings are unlocked".
- **Gold:** every solver's `gold-awarded` calls the ledger's `grantGold` (reason `ruin`, key `String(island)`), so it's once per player per ruin by the ledger's own keys.
- **HUD:** at an island, the ruin state (locked, unlocked, solved by you), the R prompt, and then the familiar "hold E to collect".

## Acceptance

Each item names the test that proves it. Integration tests use headless clients through the real room.

1. **Locking and unlocking:** sources are locked at start; collection is refused until the ruin is solved; the first solve unlocks the island for everyone, once. Integration tests.
2. **Solving:**
   - a correct answer solves and pays 40 once;
   - a second solver gets their own 40;
   - a repeat solve pays nothing;
   - a wrong answer locks that player out for 3 s, and not others;
   - leaving and reopening keeps the lockout;
   - casting off, a duel or a disconnect closes the session;
   - `checkLedger` holds.
   Integration tests.
3. **Hidden information on raw messages:** the clue goes only to the opener, the answer never, and other players get nothing but the unlocked state. Integration test.
4. **Seeds:** the ruins seed is derived from the master secret, distinct from the other systems' seeds and independent of the match code. Unit test.
5. **UI:** web unit tests for the clue rendering model (tablets and hints; the grid) and for answer entry (clicks and keys 1–6, arrows and WASD, undo).
6. **Browser scenario `ruin-solve`:**
   - one browser moored at an island opens the ruin with R and reads the clue from the page;
   - the test derives the answer from the displayed clue only, like a reader;
   - it submits, and sees "+40 gold" and the unlock;
   - it holds E to collect the rubbing.
   The test pins the ruin kind for the island through a test-only setting and covers the sequence kind; a second, untagged test covers navigation.
7. The existing scenarios still pass: `theft-loop` and `full-match` solve their islands' ruins through the same UI or a test-only unlock setting. Document which.
8. `docs/architecture.md` updated within half a page.
9. **Carried from `match-online`'s approving reviews:**
   - `MatchRoom`'s module-level `outcomes` array is bounded: it keeps the last N results, or records only under test hooks. A unit test proves it doesn't grow without limit.
   - The flow HUD banner re-arms its 7 s hide when a new reveal arrives, and hides itself after `BANNER_MS`. Both get a web unit test (fake timers) and a row in `docs/match-online-coverage.md`.
10. **The branch table:** `docs/ruins-online-coverage.md` has one row for each room-level and UI branch this feature adds or changes: the file and function, the branch, and the test that fails when the branch is deleted. Build it by deleting each branch on a scratch copy; don't commit those edits. A branch with no failing test gets a new test. # Task: game

## Goal

Make the islands' rubbings something you earn with your head, not just your hands. Each regular island's sources start **locked** behind its ruin (§3). A captain moored at the island opens the ruin and reads the clue at the site:
- **a three-symbol sequence:** six carved tablets with relational hints;
- **a small navigation puzzle:** a 4 × 4 grid.

They enter the answer. The first player to solve it unlocks the island's rubbings for everyone, and every solver earns 40 gold once. A wrong answer locks that player out for 3 s. A fresh ruin should take about 20–40 s including the 6 s rubbing, so the UI must make the clue easy to read and the answer quick to enter, and guessing must be worse than reading. The pure rules are on `main` (`packages/simulation/src/ruins`, `docs/ruins.md`); this feature wires them in.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §3 ("Exploration activities"), §11 (fresh ruin completion: 40 gold once per player per ruin) and §16 (hidden information).
- Read `docs/ruins.md` (`createRuins`, `openRuin`, `answerRuin`, leaving and duel handling, `clueFor`, the `sources-unlocked` and `gold-awarded` events, lockouts per player and ruin), `docs/objectives.md` (`unlockSource`, `grantGold` with reason `ruin` and key `String(island)`), `docs/architecture.md`, and the room and client as `match-online` left them: the master secret and per-system seeds, the lobby and phases, and how collection works at docks.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. The pure modules and their content aren't owned: use them through their exports, and report `blocked` naming the gap if a change is truly needed. Server authoritative, zod-validated messages, protocol version bump. One Phaser game per page. Tests drive input like players do, and the browser test reads the clue from the page and solves it the way a player would.
- Hidden information: a ruin's clue goes only to players moored at that island with an open session. The answer never leaves the server in any form. Other players see only whether the island is unlocked, when they're in sight of it or moored there.

## Design (settled)

- **Seeds:** the ruins get their own seed derived from the match's master secret, the `match-online` mechanism. This fixes the ruins reviewer's finding that `seed ^ const` let clues leak the ledger seed.
- **Locking:** at match start every ledger source is locked (`rubbings-theft` unlocked them all as a stopgap; remove that). Collection at an island needs its ruin solved by anyone: the first solve's `sources-unlocked` calls `unlockSource` for each.
- **Interaction:** moored at an island whose ruin this player hasn't solved, pressing **R** (a new key, shown in the HUD) opens the ruin panel. `openRuin` returns only the clue. Casting off, entering a duel or disconnecting closes the session, as the rules define. The panel shows the clue clearly:
  - **sequence:** six tablets with their symbols and hint sentences, and the answer entered by clicking three symbols in order, or keys 1–6, with an undo;
  - **navigation:** the grid drawn with start, goal and blocked cells, and the answer entered with the arrow keys or WASD, shown as a path, with an undo.
  - Submit sends `answer-ruin`: zod-validated, rate-limited, idempotent by request id.
  - A wrong answer shows the 3 s lockout counting down.
  - Solving shows "Ruin solved: +40 gold", and, if first, "The island's rubbings are unlocked".
- **Gold:** every solver's `gold-awarded` calls the ledger's `grantGold` (reason `ruin`, key `String(island)`), so it's once per player per ruin by the ledger's own keys.
- **HUD:** at an island, the ruin state (locked, unlocked, solved by you), the R prompt, and then the familiar "hold E to collect".

   - a repeat solve pays nothing;
   - a wrong answer locks that player out for 3 s, and not others;
   - leaving and reopening keeps the lockout;
   - casting off, a duel or a disconnect closes the session;
   - `checkLedger` holds.

3. **Hidden information on raw messages:** the clue goes only to the opener, the answer never, and other players get nothing but the unlocked state. Integration test.

scenarios.description: One browser creates a private match from the landing page; the HUD shows the code, the protocol version, one player and a connected status.
Two browsers join the same private match with their ships in sight of each other; one sails with the keyboard and the other browser's view shows that ship at the new server-authoritative position.
A browser sails its ship around a shoal to an island dock with the keyboard and docks there; the HUD shows the dock and the ship stops at it.
Two browsers in one match with their ships out of sight of each other: neither view lists or draws the other ship until one sails within the sight radius, and it disappears again when it sails away.

One browser opens a practice duel against the dummy, lands a jab and then a keyboard throw (J then K a frame apart); the dummy's health bar and the HUD drop by the move data's damage, and hitboxes can be shown.

Two browsers: one creates a duel, the other joins by its code; after the countdown the first lands a strike on the second, and both views show the same authoritative health, round clock and result, with the connection line showing input delay and corrections.

Two browsers in one match are placed within grapple range; the host sails at the guest and presses J; both see the grapple telegraph, then a three-second countdown and the arena; the duel is decided; the winner returns to the sea with protection shown, and the loser sees a respawn countdown and then their ship at a dock.

Two browsers moored at different islands each hold E and collect a different rubbing type; the host grapples the guest at sea, wins the duel by tapping attack keys, and picks the guest's type within five seconds; the host's HUD shows both types and more gold, the guest's shows the loss.

Two browsers: the host starts a private match from the lobby, both see the ready countdown and the match timer; the host collects both rubbing types, sees the full-set reveal and the route, sails to the final island's claim tile and holds E for ten seconds; both browsers show the results with the host as the winner.

Two browsers start a private match from the lobby with test-only short timings; nobody claims; the timer runs out; both browsers show the results with the no-winner deadline headline, and the route compass is shown inactive while no route is known.

One browser moored at an island opens its ruin with R and reads the clue from the page; the test derives the answer from the displayed clue only, submits it, sees '+40 gold' and the island unlocked, then holds E to collect the rubbing.

completion.summary: Wired the pure ruins into MatchRoom (protocol v8). Every source now starts locked (the rubbings-theft unlock-all is removed). The ruins are dealt from their own master-secret seed (deriveSeed 'ruins'). The first solve's sources-unlocked calls unlockSource, and each solver's gold-awarded calls grantGold (reason ruin, key String(island)). The room reports presence every tick in play, so casting off, a duel or a disconnect closes the session, and a leave closes it at once. New zod-validated messages: open-ruin/ruin-clue (the clue goes to the opener only, strictly parsed) and answer-ruin/ruin-result (idempotent by request id, the last 16 remembered; opens and answers share a cap of 8/s; read only in play). Private status carries the ruin state, session and lockout. Per-island ruin markers are view-filtered by sight. Test-only ruins (env PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_RUINS, the next-match route, MatchTuning.testRuins) open islands or pin a kind through derived ruins:<n> seeds. Integration quickStart and the browser server open every island, so theft-loop and full-match use the test-only unlock. Web: ruinPanel.ts (tablets with inscriptions, 4x4 grid, keys 1-6 / arrows / WASD / Backspace / Enter / Escape, clicks, lockout countdown, '+40 gold' and unlock lines), R in the HUD, neutral helm while the panel is open. Carried P2s: recordedOutcomes is bounded to 64 (outcomes.ts, with a unit test), and the banner re-arm and auto-hide have fake-timer tests plus rows 286-288 in match-online-coverage.md. docs/ruins-online-coverage.md has 188 rows (159 tested, 15 equivalent, 14 removed), each built by deleting the branch on scratch copies in parallel lanes. Checks executed here: npm run typecheck (pass), npm run test:unit (1311 pass), npm run test:integration (115 pass, 175 s), npm run build (pass, including the smoke), the full playwright suite with the JSON reporter (13 pass), and check-report (all 11 scenarios ok).
open_assumptions: An island is 'in sight' when the nearest point of its rectangle is within the sight radius. The marker is placed at the island's centre.
Opening a ruin that someone else already unlocked is still offered (R), because solving it pays that player's own 40 gold.
docs/ruins.md (not an owned path) still says the ruins aren't wired into MatchRoom. It needs a one-line update by its owner.

The e2e scenarios other than ruin-solve run with every island open (PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_RUINS=*=open in the Playwright config). ruin-solve and the navigation test ask for locked ruins through the next-match route.
completion.verify_yourself: Play one match with no test settings (npm run dev without PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_RUINS) and check that a fresh ruin takes about 20-40 s including the 6 s rubbing, reading the clue from the panel as a real player would. The timing claim rests on the pure module's reader/guesser analysis and on the browser test, not on a human playtest.
